items.value: FDI is largely a non-debt creating capital inflow
items.reasoning: The defining feature of Foreign Direct Investment is that the foreign investor takes an equity stake and shares in the enterprise's profits and losses; there is no fixed repayment obligation, so no external debt is created. This is why the RBI and the Economic Survey routinely describe FDI as the most stable, non-debt-creating component of the capital account. C is its opposite, since debt-servicing belongs to external commercial borrowings and other loan flows. A is wrong because FDI is made in both listed and unlisted companies, and investment through capital instruments in a listed company below the 10 per cent threshold is Foreign Portfolio Investment, not FDI. D describes FPI in government securities.

items.value: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct — merchandise imports exceed exports, services exports exceed services imports, and India runs an overall current account deficit
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: India is a structural merchandise trade deficit country, driven by crude oil, gold and electronics imports. Statement 3 is correct: India runs a large services trade surplus, led by software and business services. Statement 4 is correct: the services surplus and remittances do not fully offset the merchandise gap, so the overall trade and current account balance remains in deficit. Statement 2 is wrong: imports of iron and steel, chemicals, fertilisers and machinery have broadly risen, not decreased, in recent years. Only D combines 1, 3 and 4 while excluding 2.

items.value: West Texas Intermediate is a grade of crude oil
items.reasoning: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) is a light, sweet crude oil produced in the United States and is one of the world's three main crude benchmarks, alongside Brent and Dubai/Oman. It is quoted on the NYMEX and is the pricing reference most often cited in news reports of oil prices. It has nothing to do with bullion, rare earths or uranium, none of which are graded under that name.

items.value: All three — housing loans, credit card outstandings and Treasury bills are all borrowings of non-financial sectors
items.reasoning: Non-financial debt is classified by who owes it, not by who holds it: it is the total debt of households, non-financial corporations and the government, as distinct from debt owed by banks and other financial intermediaries. Housing loans and credit card outstandings are household borrowings, so 1 and 2 qualify. Treasury bills are short-term borrowings of the Government of India, and government is a non-financial sector, so 3 qualifies as well. All three therefore belong to non-financial debt.

items.value: Reactors running on imported uranium are placed under safeguards; those on domestic fuel are not
items.reasoning: Under the 2006 Separation Plan that flowed from the India–US civil nuclear agreement, India separated its civilian and strategic nuclear facilities and offered the civilian ones for IAEA safeguards. The practical dividing line is fuel: reactors fuelled with imported uranium, and the imported fuel itself, must be under safeguards so that the supplier can verify it is not diverted to weapons use, whereas reactors run on indigenous uranium remain outside safeguards. A is wrong because thorium is not the criterion; C and D are wrong because ownership is irrelevant — India's power reactors are all operated by NPCIL, a State-owned entity, yet only some are safeguarded.

items.value: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — TRIMS bars quantitative import restrictions on enterprises and does not itself regulate foreign investment
items.reasoning: Statement 2 is decisively wrong: Article 1 of the TRIMS Agreement states that it applies to investment measures related to trade in goods only, so services are outside its scope. That single point eliminates options A, B and D, all of which include statement 2. Statement 1 is correct because Article 2 forbids TRIMs inconsistent with GATT Article XI, and the Illustrative List names measures restricting an enterprise's imports. Statement 3 is correct in the sense the WTO itself uses: TRIMS disciplines investment measures that distort trade in goods, but it does not regulate the entry, ownership or conduct of foreign investment as such.

items.value: Only measure 2 — raising the Marginal Standing Facility rate — is what an expansionist RBI would not do
items.reasoning: The question asks what the RBI would NOT do under an expansionary stance. Cutting the SLR (1) frees bank resources for lending, and cutting the Bank Rate and Repo Rate (3) lowers the cost of funds; both are expansionary and would be done. Raising the MSF rate (2) makes emergency overnight borrowing from the RBI dearer and tightens liquidity, which is contractionary and therefore the one action an expansionist RBI would avoid. Hence only 2 belongs in the answer.

items.value: Statements 3 and 4 are correct — the rural non-farm economy grew faster while the growth rate of rural employment fell
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is wrong: worker productivity rose in rural areas too, not only in urban areas, as rural workers shifted out of low-productivity agriculture. Statement 2 is wrong: the rural share of the workforce has fallen steadily since 1991 with urbanisation and migration, the opposite of a steady increase. Statement 3 is correct: construction, trade and services expanded sharply in rural areas, and the non-farm share of rural employment rose. Statement 4 is correct: overall rural employment growth decelerated after liberalisation, most visibly between 2004-05 and 2011-12. Runner-up C, which accepts 3 but rejects 4, is the plausible alternative if one reads statement 4 as referring to the non-farm segment alone.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct — DCCBs mainly finance PACS, but they are not the largest short-term agricultural lender
items.reasoning: Statement 2 is correct: the District Central Cooperative Bank is the middle tier of the three-tier short-term cooperative credit structure, and refinancing the Primary Agricultural Credit Societies below it is its core function. Statement 1 is wrong: Scheduled Commercial Banks dominate agricultural credit delivery in India, accounting for roughly three-quarters of the ground-level credit flow, while the cooperative sector's share has shrunk to well under a fifth. So DCCBs deliver far less short-term agricultural credit than commercial banks, not more.

items.value: Items 1, 3 and 4 are covered; the cost of a new computer physically damaged by a miscreant is not
items.reasoning: Individual cyber insurance policies sold in India cover the consequences of cyber events: restoring or decontaminating a system after a malware attack (1), the fees of a specialist consultant engaged to contain a cyber-extortion demand (3), and legal defence costs when a third party sues the insured over a cyber incident (4). Item 2 is physical damage to hardware by a person, which is a peril for a householder's or property policy, not a cyber policy — cyber cover responds to digital harm, not to a smashed machine. Hence 1, 3 and 4 only.

items.value: Items 2, 3 and 6 — computerisation of PACS, social capital development and government cold storages are capital investment, the rest are subsidies or price support
items.reasoning: Public investment in agriculture means government spending that creates durable assets or capacity. Computerising Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (2) builds institutional infrastructure, social capital development (3) builds durable institutional capacity, and setting up cold storages (6) creates physical assets — all investment. Fixing the Minimum Support Price (1) is a price-support instrument, free electricity (4) is an input subsidy, and loan waivers (5) are a fiscal transfer; none of the three creates an asset, and in the Economic Survey's own framing they are precisely the revenue-side subsidies that crowd out public investment in agriculture.

items.value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; statement 3 inverts the ratio's meaning
items.reasoning: The Interest Coverage Ratio is earnings before interest and tax divided by interest expense, so it measures how many times over a firm can pay the interest on its borrowings. A bank uses it both to gauge a borrower's present repayment capacity (1) and, by tracking its trend, to spot deteriorating or emerging risk before default (2). Statement 3 reverses the relationship: a higher ratio means a larger earnings cushion over interest and therefore a better, not worse, ability to service debt.

items.value: All four — MSP, government trading, government stockpiling and consumer subsidies have all influenced rice prices
items.reasoning: The Minimum Support Price (1) sets an effective floor for paddy and shapes farmers' price expectations. Government trading (2) — procurement by FCI and state agencies, open market sales and export decisions — directly moves the quantity available in the market. Stockpiling (3) withdraws grain into buffer stocks and its release adds supply back, both of which alter market prices. Consumer subsidies (4) supply rice cheaply through the PDS, shifting a large share of demand off the open market and depressing open-market prices. All four are operative, so D.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct — textiles are an important item of India–Bangladesh trade
items.reasoning: Statement 2 is correct: India is a major supplier of cotton and yarn to Bangladesh's garment industry, and textiles and textile articles are among the leading items in the bilateral basket in both directions. Statement 3 is wrong: Bangladesh, not Nepal, has been India's largest trading partner in South Asia. Statement 1 is wrong because of the word 'consistently' — Indo–Sri Lanka trade has trended upward over the decade but fell in individual years, so it has not increased consistently. Since 3 is clearly false and 2 clearly true, the choice turns entirely on statement 1, and the strict reading of 'consistently' rules it out; A is the runner-up if the statement is read loosely as a broad upward trend.

items.value: Argentina, Mexico, South Africa and Turkey — all four are G20 members
items.reasoning: The G20 comprises nineteen member countries plus the European Union. Argentina, Mexico, South Africa and Turkey are all among the nineteen, so A is fully correct. B fails because Malaysia and New Zealand are not members. C fails because Iran and Vietnam are not members. D fails because Singapore is not a member, though it is frequently invited as a guest — which is exactly the trap in that option.

items.value: Purposes 1, 3 and 4 — farm asset maintenance working capital, household consumption needs and post-harvest expenses
items.reasoning: The short-term component of the Kisan Credit Card covers crop cultivation costs, post-harvest expenses (4), produce marketing loans, the consumption requirements of the farmer's household (3), and working capital for maintenance of farm assets and allied activities (1). Purchase of combine harvesters, tractors and mini trucks (2) and construction of a family house or a cold storage (5) are capital expenditures financed under the separate investment or term-credit component, not short-term credit. Hence 1, 3 and 4 only.

items.value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the RBI's key inflation measure is CPI, not WPI
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: food and beverages carry a weight of roughly 46 per cent in the CPI against about 24 per cent for food articles and products in the WPI. Statement 2 is correct: the WPI basket covers only goods traded at the wholesale level and excludes services altogether, while the CPI includes services such as education, health and transport. Statement 3 is wrong and is the reverse of what happened — following the Urjit Patel Committee and the adoption of flexible inflation targeting in 2016, the RBI uses headline CPI as its nominal anchor for policy rate decisions.

items.value: Pairs 3 and 4 are correct — Volga to the Caspian Sea and Zambezi to the Indian Ocean
items.reasoning: The Volga is the longest river of Europe and drains into the Caspian Sea near Astrakhan, so pair 3 is correct. The Zambezi crosses southern Africa and empties into the Indian Ocean through its delta in Mozambique, so pair 4 is correct. Pair 1 is wrong: the Mekong ends in a delta on the South China Sea in southern Vietnam, not the Andaman Sea. Pair 2 is wrong: the Thames flows east through London into the North Sea, while the Irish Sea lies on England's western side.

items.value: Neither statement is correct
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is wrong: open-ended procurement at MSP applies in practice only to paddy and wheat and only in the states where FCI and state agencies operate; for pulses and oilseeds, procurement under the Price Support Scheme is capped at a fixed share of a state's production and is triggered only when market prices fall below MSP. Statement 2 is wrong on its face: the MSP is a floor, not a ceiling, and market prices for cereals and pulses frequently rise well above it — the guarantee runs the other way, that the government will buy if prices fall below MSP.

items.value: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — commercial paper is a short-term unsecured promissory note and call money is short-term interbank finance
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: commercial paper is an unsecured money-market promissory note issued at a discount by corporates, primary dealers and financial institutions for tenors from seven days to one year. Statement 3 is correct: call money is uncollateralised overnight borrowing and lending, overwhelmingly between banks. Statement 2 is wrong twice over — a Certificate of Deposit is a short-term instrument and is issued by banks and select financial institutions, not by the RBI. Statement 4 is wrong: a zero-coupon bond pays no periodic interest at all and is issued at a discount to face value, which is precisely why it is called zero-coupon.

items.value: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct — Parivrajaka is a wandering renunciant and Upasaka is a Buddhist lay follower
items.reasoning: Parivrajaka literally means one who wanders forth, and in the sixth-century BCE ferment it denoted an ascetic who had renounced household life and moved from place to place, so pair 1 is correct. Upasaka (feminine upasika) is the standard term for a lay devotee of the Buddha who takes the refuges and precepts but does not join the sangha, so pair 3 is correct. Pair 2 is wrong: the Shramana was a wandering ascetic of the heterodox traditions who rejected Vedic ritual and Brahmanical authority — the antithesis of a high-status priest, which would be the Brahmana.

items.value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — the herd is led by a matriarch and gestation can reach 22 months
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: elephant herds are matriarchal, led by the oldest experienced female, while adult bulls live singly or in loose bachelor groups. Statement 2 is correct: elephant gestation is the longest of any land mammal, running about 18 to 22 months. Statement 3 is wrong: cows continue to calve well beyond 40, into their late fifties and sixties. Statement 4 is wrong: Karnataka holds the largest elephant population among Indian states, with Assam next; Kerala is not the highest.

items.value: Nagarhole, Sathyamangalam and Wayanad lie in the Cauvery basin; Papikonda does not
items.reasoning: Nagarhole National Park in Karnataka is drained by the Kabini, and Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary in Kerala lies at the Kabini's headwaters — the Kabini flows east and joins the Cauvery, so both 1 and 4 are in the Cauvery basin. Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve in Tamil Nadu is drained by the Bhavani and Moyar, both Cauvery tributaries, so 3 qualifies. Papikonda National Park (2) lies on the Godavari in Andhra Pradesh, an entirely different basin, which rules out options A and D.

items.value: All four named species are birds
items.reasoning: The Ceylon frogmouth is a nocturnal bird of the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka; the coppersmith barbet is the familiar crimson-breasted barbet whose metallic call gives it its name; the gray-chinned minivet is a small brightly coloured passerine of the eastern Himalaya; and the white-throated redstart is a Himalayan chat. All four are avian, and the giveaway is that barbet, minivet and redstart are each a standard bird-family name.

items.value: Kanha National Park, home of the hard-ground barasingha
items.reasoning: The hard-ground barasingha, Rucervus duvaucelii branderi, survives in the wild only in Kanha National Park in Madhya Pradesh, where it grazes on the open maidans and, unlike the swamp-dwelling nominate subspecies, has hooves adapted to firm ground and feeds exclusively on grasses. It is Kanha's flagship species and its recovery from a few dozen animals is the park's best-known conservation success. Manas is associated with the pygmy hog and hispid hare, Mudumalai with elephants and tigers, and Tal Chhapar with blackbuck.
